subproblem.title: Cell structure of L_n near a compact set K: finitely many faces meeting K, closedness of L_n, Hⁿ(L_{n−1}) = 0 and Hⁿ-a.e. covering of L_n ∩ K by their open faces (Simon Ch. 6, 5.1 and (26)–(33); steps 1(b), 1(c), 2 of the parent proof)
subproblem.statement: Conventions (as in the selected node): ℝ^P = Euclid P, ℝⁿ = Euclid n, Hᵈ = μHE[d], e_i = EuclideanSpace.single i 1 ∈ ℝ^P, x_i the i-th coordinate. n := m + 1. For a pair p = (z, ι) ∈ ℤ^P × (Fin n → Fin P): Φ_p(y) := z + Σ_{j<n} y_j e_{ι(j)} for y ∈ ℝⁿ (Lean: WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.1 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.2 j) (1 : ℝ)); e_p := (e_{ι(0)}, …, e_{ι(m)}); Q₁ := {y ∈ ℝⁿ : 0 < y_i < 1 for all i} with Lebesgue measure (volume); F_p := {x ∈ ℝ^P : z_i ≤ x_i ≤ z_i + 1 for i ∈ range ι, x_i = z_i for i ∉ range ι} (the closed unit face of the selected node's statement); A_p := Φ_p(Q₁) (the open face). 𝒟^d(U) = TestFormOn U d and 𝒟_d(U) = GeometricCurrentOn U d (domain univ throughout); ∂X = X.boundary; M_W(X) = X.massOn W and M(X) = X.mass (Euclidean coefficient norm covectorEuclideanNorm); IMRep and IsIntegerMultiplicity are the contract notions. Statement: let P, m ∈ ℕ with n = m + 1 < P, K ⊆ ℝ^P compact, and L_n := {x ∈ ℝ^P : there is a finset t of coordinate indices with P ≤ m + 1 + |t| and x_i ∈ ℤ for i ∈ t}. Then there is a finite set s of pairs p = (z, ι) ∈ ℤ^P × (Fin n → Fin P) such that: ι is strictly increasing for every p ∈ s; F_p ⊆ cthickening(√P, K) for every p ∈ s; L_n is closed; and for μHE[n]-almost every x ∈ L_n ∩ K (a.e. for μHE[n]⌞(L_n ∩ K)) there are p ∈ s and y ∈ Q₁ with Φ_p(y) = x.
subproblem.lean_statement: ∀ (P m : ℕ) (K : Set (Euclid P)), m + 1 < P → IsCompact K → ∃ s : Finset ((Fin P → ℤ) × (Fin (m + 1) → Fin P)), (∀ p ∈ s, StrictMono p.2) ∧ (∀ p ∈ s, {x : Euclid P | ∀ i : Fin P, (i ∈ Set.range p.2 → (p.1 i : ℝ) ≤ x i ∧ x i ≤ p.1 i + 1) ∧ (i ∉ Set.range p.2 → x i = p.1 i)} ⊆ cthickening (Real.sqrt P) K) ∧ IsClosed {x : Euclid P | ∃ t : Finset (Fin P), P ≤ m + 1 + t.card ∧ ∀ i ∈ t, ∃ z : ℤ, x i = z} ∧ ∀ᵐ x ∂(μHE[m + 1].restrict ({x : Euclid P | ∃ t : Finset (Fin P), P ≤ m + 1 + t.card ∧ ∀ i ∈ t, ∃ z : ℤ, x i = z} ∩ K)), ∃ p ∈ s, ∃ y : Euclid (m + 1), (∀ i, 0 < y i ∧ y i < 1) ∧ WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => (p.1 i : ℝ)) + ∑ j, y j • EuclideanSpace.single (p.2 j) (1 : ℝ) = x
subproblem.natural_proof:
Source: Simon Ch. 6, proof of 5.1 (the faces F ∈ 𝓛_n of the grid, and displays (26)–(33), where Hⁿ(L_{n−1}) = 0 is used when Q is decomposed over the open faces), as used in steps 1(b), 1(c) and 2 of the parent proof (every point of L_n ∖ L_{n−1} lies in exactly one open face, only finitely many faces meet the compact K, diam F_p ≤ √P, Hⁿ(L_{n−1}) = 0). Dependency: FG = sibling dor_lmb_fcd_fr_face_geometry. n := m + 1, and L' := {x : there is a finset t with P ≤ m + |t| and x_i ∈ ℤ for i ∈ t} (the (n−1)-skeleton L_{n−1}: points with at least P − m integer coordinates).

0. Hⁿ(L') = 0, i.e. μHE[m+1](L') = 0. (This is the argument of the comparator-accepted DAG declaration cmcdtfr_skeleton_null, whose frozen type is exactly this equation; its Lean proof is in candidate commit 09516d6d883db6c4d6e24410e2a32da5a8ae36f4 and may be copied, but only as a local `have` inside this theorem's proof: do not add a top-level declaration named cmcdtfr_skeleton_null or any other cmcdtfr_* name, which belong to another DAG branch.) μH[d] is Mathlib's unnormalized d-dimensional Hausdorff measure and μHE[d] = c_d • μH[d] for a constant c_d (Measure.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_def), so it suffices to show μH[m+1](L') = 0.
 (a) Countable cover. For a finset t and z : Fin P → ℤ let A(t, z) := {x : x_i = z_i for i ∈ t}. If x ∈ L' with witness t, choose z with x_i = z_i for i ∈ t; then x ∈ A(t, z). So L' ⊆ ⋃_{t : P ≤ m + |t|} ⋃_{z : Fin P → ℤ} A(t, z), a countable union (finitely many t; Fin P → ℤ is countable), and by countable subadditivity (measure_iUnion_null, measure_mono_null) it suffices that μH[m+1](A(t, z)) = 0 for each t with P ≤ m + |t| and each z.
 (b) Parametrization. Fix such t, z. S := {i : Fin P // i ∉ t} has r := P − |t| ≤ m elements (Fintype.card_subtype_compl). Let g : (S → ℝ) → ℝ^P, g(w) := WithLp.toLp 2 (fun i => if h : i ∈ t then (z i : ℝ) else w ⟨i, h⟩). For the sup metrics, w ↦ (i ↦ g(w)_i) is 1-Lipschitz into Fin P → ℝ (each coordinate is constant or a coordinate of w: dist_le_pi_dist, dist_pi_le_iff), and WithLp.toLp 2 is Lipschitz (PiLp.lipschitzWith_toLp); so g is K-Lipschitz for some K. A(t, z) ⊆ g(univ): for x ∈ A(t, z) take w_⟨j,h⟩ := x_j.
 (c) On S → ℝ, μH[card S] = volume (hausdorffMeasure_pi_real), so every ball B(0, k) has finite μH[r]-measure (measure_ball_lt_top). As r < m + 1, Measure.hausdorffMeasure_zero_or_top (d₁ = r < d₂ = m + 1) gives μH[m+1](B(0, k)) = 0; univ = ⋃_{k∈ℕ} B(0, k) (Metric.iUnion_ball_nat), so μH[m+1](univ : Set (S → ℝ)) = 0.
 (d) μH[m+1](g(univ)) ≤ K^{m+1}·μH[m+1](univ) = 0 (LipschitzWith.hausdorffMeasure_image_le), hence μH[m+1](A(t, z)) = 0. By (a), μH[m+1](L') = 0, and μHE[m+1](L') = c_{m+1} • 0 = 0 (Measure.smul_apply). This covers P ≤ m (t = ∅ is a witness and L' = ℝ^P) and P = 0.

1. L_n is closed. L_n = ⋃_{t : P ≤ n + |t|} ⋂_{i∈t} {x : x_i ∈ ℤ}. Each {x : x_i ∈ ℤ} is the preimage of the closed set ℤ ⊆ ℝ (the range of Int.cast, closed because distinct integers are at distance ≥ 1) under the continuous coordinate map x ↦ x_i. Finite intersections, and the finite union over the finitely many finsets t ⊆ Fin P, of closed sets are closed.

2. The finite family. Let 𝒫 := {p = (z, ι) : ι strictly increasing and F_p ∩ K ≠ ∅}. K is bounded, so there is R ≥ 0 with |x_i| ≤ R for all x ∈ K and all i. If x ∈ F_p ∩ K, then z_i ≤ x_i ≤ z_i + 1 for i ∈ range ι, giving |z_i| ≤ R + 1, and z_i = x_i for i ∉ range ι, giving |z_i| ≤ R. Hence 𝒫 ⊆ {z ∈ ℤ^P : |z_i| ≤ R + 1 for all i} × (Fin n → Fin P), a product of two finite sets; so 𝒫 is finite. Let s be the finset with elements 𝒫. Every p ∈ s has ι strictly increasing.

3. Thickening. Let p ∈ s and choose k ∈ F_p ∩ K. For x ∈ F_p, FG(7) gives dist(x, k) ≤ √P, so x ∈ cthickening(√P, K) (Metric.mem_cthickening_of_dist_le). Hence F_p ⊆ cthickening(√P, K).

4. Points of (L_n ∩ K) ∖ L' lie in open faces of s. Let x ∈ L_n ∩ K with x ∉ L'. Let S := {i : x_i ∉ ℤ} and T := {i : x_i ∈ ℤ}, the complement of S. Since x ∈ L_n there is t with P ≤ n + |t| and x_i ∈ ℤ for i ∈ t, i.e. t ⊆ T; so |T| ≥ P − n. Since x ∉ L', the finset T (all of whose coordinates are integers) does not satisfy P ≤ m + |T|, so |T| ≤ P − m − 1 = P − n. Hence |T| = P − n and |S| = n. Let ι : Fin n → Fin P be the strictly increasing enumeration of S (Finset.orderEmbOfFin), so range ι = S. Put z_i := ⌊x_i⌋ for all i and y_k := x_{ι(k)} − ⌊x_{ι(k)}⌋ (fractional part) for k < n; since x_{ι(k)} ∉ ℤ, 0 < y_k < 1, so y ∈ Q₁. For p := (z, ι), Φ_p(y) = x: since ι is injective, the coordinate of Φ_p(y) at ι(k) is z_{ι(k)} + y_k = x_{ι(k)}, and at i ∉ S it is z_i = ⌊x_i⌋ = x_i because x_i ∈ ℤ. By FG(5), x = Φ_p(y) ∈ F_p, and x ∈ K; so F_p ∩ K ≠ ∅ and p ∈ s.

5. The almost-everywhere statement. By step 4, the set B of x ∈ L_n ∩ K for which there are no p ∈ s and y ∈ Q₁ with Φ_p(y) = x is contained in L'. L_n ∩ K is closed (step 1; K is compact, hence closed), hence Borel, so (μHE[n]⌞(L_n ∩ K))({x : no such p, y}) = μHE[n]({x : no such p, y} ∩ L_n ∩ K) = μHE[n](B) ≤ μHE[n](L') = 0 (step 0; Measure.restrict_apply' with the Borel set L_n ∩ K). This is the claimed statement for μHE[n]⌞(L_n ∩ K)-almost every x. ∎
proof_key_steps: Hⁿ(L_{n−1}) = 0: cover L_{n−1} by the countably many coordinate planes A(t, z), each in the image of a Lipschitz map from a space of dimension P − |t| ≤ m < m + 1, and use μHE = c·μH.
L_n is a finite union of finite intersections of closed coordinate conditions x_i ∈ ℤ.
Faces meeting the bounded set K have bounded integer corners, so they form a finite set s.
diam F_p ≤ √P (face_geometry) gives F_p ⊆ cthickening(√P, K) for p ∈ s.
A point of (L_n ∩ K) ∖ L_{n−1} has exactly n non-integer coordinates and equals Φ_p(fractional parts) for p = (⌊x⌋, increasing enumeration of those coordinates) ∈ s.
Hⁿ(L_{n−1}) = 0 (step 0) gives the covering for μHE[n]⌞(L_n ∩ K)-a.e. x.
